messages:
maya: Heads-up — I'm prototyping a per-tenant SLO preview in the console that shows estimated notify fanout + sample alerts when you tweak thresholds. Need API shape feedback.

simon: nice. is this just a client-side sim or do we call a server simulation endpoint?

maya: planning server-side so we can use real telemetry (sampling weights, quiet windows, routing rules). front-end calls /slo-preview?tenant_id=...&threshold=...

ali: careful with perf — running a full fanout sim could be expensive if naive. we should avoid recomputing across all contacts for every keystroke.

nora: +1. maybe server returns a diff: {delta_count, top_destinations, expected_quota_burn}. small payload.

maya: idea: simulate against the last 7 days of synthetic signals and reuse cached sim per-tenant+threshold fingerprint. TTL 5m. cheap to compute incremental deltas.

simon: how do we surface sampling? e.g., if sampling reduces notify by 90% client needs to see that effect.

maya: include fields: sampled_estimate, raw_estimate, sampling_strategy_id. UI can show a badge "sampling applied".

ali: API contract thought: POST /slo-preview {tenant, query, threshold, lookback, sampling_overrides?} responds with {raw, sampled, top_routes:[{route, count, escalation}], signals_checked}. keep it idempotent and rate-limited.

nora: we should also include a cost_estimate token:cost and a confidence score — some heuristics when historical variance is high.

maya: question about routing policies: when preview shows >1 route (region vs fallback) should we surface which route will actually get paged? routing resolution happens after capacity filters. do we model capacity?

simon: modeling capacity makes sims heavy. propose we model routing deterministically by policy order, with a flag to "include capacity fallbacks" which runs a cheaper fallback heuristic.

ali: implementation note: don't resolve contacts by calling internal notify service for every sim. we should query a compact index: tenant->route_map snapshot. snapshot updated on notify-policy changes.

maya: agree. also need privacy guardrails — previews must not expose contact identifiers in UI snapshots for users without access. show anonymized buckets like "pager on-call x2".

nora: telemetry: emit slo_preview.request, with tags {tenant_id_hash, threshold, lookback, sampling_override}. also emit slo_preview.estimate with fields (raw, sampled, top_routes). keep sizes small for metrics storage.

simon: what about rollout UX? we want preview to tie into canary rollouts for default thresholds. after preview, user can save an experiment that will apply to 5% of tenants. API should return experiment_id so console can link.

maya: good call. flow: preview -> create-experiment POST /slo-experiments {baseline, candidate, percent, duration} -> returns id + simulation for estimated global impact.

ali: edge-case: if preview uses stale snapshot and experiment applies immediately, mismatch could surprise users. add "snapshot_version" in preview and require experiment create to include snapshot_version or force a fresh re-sim.

nora: ops concern — sims will add load. can we batch preview requests and compute asynchronously with a small queue? UI poll or websocket when done?

maya: let's do immediate quick estimate for interactive feedback (fast path) and enqueue full-fidelity job for detailed breakdown. UI shows "quick estimate" vs "full estimate (ready in ~10s)".

simon: think about rate limits: per-user and per-tenant caps. we'd want to prevent mass replays from scripts.

deploy-bot: note: deploy window 02:00-03:00 UTC tonight. any infra changes requiring DB migrations should be scheduled.

maya: action items: (1) ali to sketch API proto + rate limit rules, (2) sim team (nora) to define snapshot format and telemetry fields, (3) sim UX (maya) to wire quick vs full paths and anonymization.

ali: I'll throw up a minimal OpenAPI snippet in this thread by EOD.

nora: I'll prototype snapshot schema and a small cost-estimate function.

maya: thanks — will collate and create a tiny RFC. :thumbsup:
